Summary
Jack, currently stationed in Manila, Philippines, writes to inform his recipients of his new location and to share his experiences in the region, including visits to various army bases and encounters with jungle environments. He also describes the destruction left behind by Japanese forces in Manila and the ongoing efforts of Filipinos and U.S. Army to rebuild the city. Jack expresses hope to share more details and photos in future letters.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_33a) --- Dear Folks: You'll notice I'm leaving Ruth off the letter heading this time. You'll also notice that I haven't written for a little while and that I'm now in Manila in the Philippine Islands. Just arrived here and I'm rushing off these few words to let you know where I'm at. Naturally there are loads of things to tell but I can't give you all the details in this one letter. Will have to spread it out at least over a few of them. There are many changes to relate to you. Note the new address. I've been changed on APO's so fast I don't think the old mail will ever catch up. However, they had a letter of yours today dated 12 which was addressed to APO 121 so I have some hope of getting off on this. I'll let you know later on how it goes. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_33b) --- Australia came here first. States as a sort of central. Therefore the boys tell me is. made from the State arrives. We. mi 10 days or less. Left [illegible] Brisbane a while ago by airplane. We made plenty of stops on the way up and I thus added quite a number of areas and bases to my travels. Many new experiences and ran into quite a few army friends here and [illegible] at the Islands in New Guinea. Rode in some models of airplanes I hadn't been in before. Didn't take any pictures this time because all of the jungle bases look the same. Once you've seen one of those places, you've seen them all. The heat, vegetation, the mud and mosquitoes. Always the same as the pictures I've already sent you. I collected some [illegible] & file d [illegible] --- Page 3 (Beckerman_33c) --- also saw photos of things such as knocked out tanks and ammunition And a collection of sea Manila is a very peculiar and almost weird place at the moment. The plunder and ruin that the Japs left behind have to be seen to be believed. The city is in ruined but the Filipinos are busy at work on reconstruction jobs. The U.S. Army is everywhere. I've seen hundreds of pictures of bombed and wrecked cities but this is the first time I've seen the real thing - and it's brutal in the worst sense of the word. Well write you a much more about it. I expect loads of new pictures soon that I'll be shipping --- Page 4 (Beckerman_33d) --- have. There's so much to say that I better wind this up or I'll never stop. Am in best of health. Everything going O.K. Hope you're all well. Love and regards Jack
